questions.question: In the PERPETUAL system, a credit sale fires:
options: TWO entries — the selling price to Debtors and Sales, and at the same moment the cost out of Trading Stock into Cost of Sales
One entry at selling price only
An entry in the Purchases account
No entry until year end

questions.question: In the PERIODIC system, goods bought are debited to:
options: Trading Stock as an asset
A PURCHASES account — an expense-type account, with Trading Stock left at its opening balance all year
Cost of Sales directly
The Bank account

questions.question: During the year, the periodic system's Trading Stock account:
options: Is updated at every sale
Shows the current shelf value daily
Stands UNTOUCHED at its opening balance — nobody knows the stock figure between counts
Is closed off monthly

questions.question: The design difference in one sentence:
options: Perpetual is for services; periodic is for goods
Perpetual counts monthly; periodic counts weekly
Perpetual uses selling prices; periodic uses cost prices
Perpetual records COST AT EVERY MOVEMENT; periodic records PURCHASES and reasons cost of sales out backwards at period end

subtopics.title: Cost of Sales in Both Systems

questions.question: Sales are R480 000 with a mark-up of 60% ON COST. Cost of sales is:
options: R300 000 — sales are 160% of cost, so 480 000 x 100/160

questions.question: The periodic formula runs:
options: Sales less purchases equals cost of sales
Opening stock + purchases + carriage on purchases - purchases returns - drawings of stock = goods available for sale; less closing stock = cost of sales
Closing stock plus purchases less opening stock
Purchases less returns equals cost of sales

questions.question: Carriage on purchases joins the calculation, but carriage outward stays out, because:
options: Carriage outward is paid by the customer
Carriage on purchases is always larger
Freight inward is part of landing stock on the shelf; delivering to customers is a SELLING expense
Only one carriage type may appear per year

questions.question: The periodic system's silent flaw is that:
options: Purchases are recorded twice
Gross profit cannot be calculated at all
Closing stock is always overstated
Stock lost to theft, breakage or error sits INSIDE cost of sales — the formula assumes everything not counted was sold, so losses are never named

questions.question: The perpetual system's decisive advantage is that:
options: The account's claim can be TESTED against a physical count, so losses are identified and measured as a deficit
It requires no bookkeeping
It removes the need for stocktakes entirely
It is always cheaper to run

questions.question: The periodic system's serious disadvantage is:
options: It cannot compute gross profit at year end
NO CONTROL — losses are invisible, absorbed silently into cost of sales, so theft can run unnoticed for a year
It doubles the number of ledger entries
It cannot handle returns

questions.question: High-value, individually identifiable items (vehicles, appliances, jewellery) argue for:
options: The periodic system, to save administration
Either system equally
The PERPETUAL system — the value of knowing and the cost of losing are both high, and the items are few enough to record
No stock records at all

questions.question: The technology argument that lifts a comparison answer:
options: Computers make the periodic count unnecessary
Spreadsheets replaced both systems
Barcodes only work for expensive goods
Point-of-sale scanning posts the cost automatically, making perpetual practical even for supermarkets — periodic now survives mainly where no such till exists

subtopics.title: Stock Control, Ethics and Internal Audit

questions.question: Physical stock controls include:
options: A locked, restricted storeroom with named responsibility; deliveries checked against order and delivery note before signing; separation of ordering, receiving, recording and paying
Letting any staff member fetch stock as needed
Keeping all records with one trusted person
Counting stock only when losses are suspected

questions.question: Stocktakes should be carried out by:
options: The storeman, who knows the stock best
People INDEPENDENT of the storeroom, with every difference investigated rather than merely noted
The supplier's delivery team
Whoever is free that day

questions.question: Overstating the closing stock figure has the effect of:
options: Raising cost of sales and lowering profit
Leaving profit unchanged
LOWERING cost of sales, so gross and net profit RISE — flattering results and rolling the loss into the following year
Reducing sales for the year

questions.question: An unexplained gap between the achieved gross profit percentage and the policy mark-up is:
options: Normal seasonal variation, never investigated
Proof of a bookkeeping error only
A reason to raise prices
Usually the first fingerprint of stock loss — which is why the internal auditor compares the two

questions.question: For every cooldrink sold, the notebook owner writes down:
options: The R25 taken AND that a bottle costing R18 left the shelf
Only the R25 taken
Only the R18 cost
Nothing until year end

questions.question: The counting owner's year-end sum is:
options: What I sold, plus what I bought, minus what I started with
Everything I started with, plus everything I bought, minus what is still here — that must be what I sold
What the till took, minus the invoices
What the shelves hold, times the mark-up

questions.question: The assumption the counting owner is quietly making is that:
options: His suppliers always deliver in full
His prices never change
Everything missing from the shelf was SOLD — so a case stolen in August is calmly called a sale
The count will match the notebook

questions.question: Opening R70 000, purchases R480 000, carriage in R15 000, returns R10 000, drawings of stock R5 000. Goods available for sale:
With closing stock counted at R88 000, cost of sales is:
Stock the owner carried home for his family is subtracted because:
options: It counts as a cash sale
It reduces the closing count
It is DRAWINGS, not a sale — it left the pile without being sold
It was returned to the supplier

questions.question: With sales of R660 000 and cost of sales of R462 000, gross profit is:

subtopics.title: Which One Should the Shop Use?

questions.question: A shop selling thousands of cheap items historically chose the counting system because:
options: Writing the cost of every item as it leaves is a full-time job that earns nothing — simple and cheap was good enough
The law once required it
Cheap items cannot be stolen
Counting is more accurate than recording

questions.question: "The notebook writes itself" refers to:
options: Hiring a bookkeeper for the till
A barcode-scanning till that takes the money AND posts the cost entry automatically
Copying last year's records forward
Estimating the cost from the mark-up

questions.question: The notebook system "lets you catch things" because:
options: It photographs each customer
It stops staff entering the storeroom
Counting the shelf against what the notebook claims gives the gap a SIZE and a NAME
It reduces the price of stock

questions.question: Inflating the closing stock count is ugly because:
options: It makes the stocktake take longer
It reduces the reported profit
It only affects the cash budget
The shelves stay just as empty while the report glows — misleading owner and bank, and the loss arrives anyway next year
